## Appeal Letter

Dear BlueSky Health Plan,

I am writing to appeal the denial of my claim for CPT 70553 (MRI Brain without Contrast) dated March 1, 2024. [S1]

The denial cites Policy Section 4.2 regarding Diagnostic Imaging; however, the requested MRI meets clinical necessity criteria under the same section. [S2]

My treating physician documented progressive headaches and neurological symptoms consistent with the coverage criteria. [S3]

I respectfully request that you reconsider this denial.

Sincerely,
Jane Smith

summary.explanation: Your MRI claim was denied under Policy Section 4.2 (Diagnostic Imaging) because the insurer determined the procedure did not meet their Medical Necessity criteria. This is one of the most commonly appealed denial categories and has a relatively high overturn rate when supported by physician documentation.

## Appeal Letter

Dear BlueSky Health Plan,

I am writing to appeal the denial of my claim for CPT 70553 (MRI Brain without Contrast) dated March 1, 2024. [S1]

The denial cites Policy Section 4.2 regarding Diagnostic Imaging; however, the requested MRI meets clinical necessity criteria under the same section. [S2]

My treating physician documented progressive headaches and neurological symptoms consistent with the coverage criteria. [S3]

I respectfully request that you reconsider this denial.

Sincerely,
Jane Smith

S1.text: MRI procedures are covered when deemed medically necessary by a licensed physician.

S2.text: Medical necessity is established when the procedure is consistent with the diagnosis and would not be performed absent the clinical indication.

S3.text: Claims for diagnostic imaging must be supported by contemporaneous physician notes documenting the clinical indication.
